label: thm:hyzz
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:hyzz}
  Let $B$ be a smooth, purely even $\Bbbk$-analytic space, let $(\mathcal{H},\nabla)/B$ be maximal at $b\in B(\Bbbk)$, and let
  $\mathcal{H}_{b,0}=\bigoplus_iH_i$ be a $K_b^{\mathrm F}$-stable decomposition with
  pairwise disjoint spectra. Then, on an admissible neighborhood
  $U\cong\prod_iU_i$ of $b$, there are maximal F-bundles
  $(\mathcal{H}_i,\nabla_i)/U_i$ with $(\mathcal{H},\nabla)|_U\cong\boxplus_i(\mathcal{H}_i,\nabla_i)$,
  inducing the prescribed decomposition of $\mathcal{H}_{b,0}$.

label: lem:reduced-spectrum
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:reduced-spectrum}
  At a rational point $b\in B_X^{\mathsf{Hod}}(\Bbbk)$, the
  operator $K_b^{\mathrm F}$ has the same distinct eigenvalues on
  $\mathrm{H}^*(X,\Bbbk)$ as on
  $H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(X)\otimes_\mathbb{Q}\Bbbk$.

label: lem:lattice-independence
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lattice-independence}
  Let $(\mathcal{M},\nabla)$ be a regular-singular meromorphic connection over
  $\Bbbk((u))$.
  \begin{enumerate}
   \item The multiset in $\Bbbk/\mathbb{Z}$ of residue eigenvalues modulo $\mathbb{Z}$, counted
   with algebraic multiplicity, does not depend on the choice of
   logarithmic lattice.
   \item Every differential submodule $\mathcal{N}\subseteq\mathcal{M}$ is regular singular.
   Its multiset of residue eigenvalues modulo $\mathbb{Z}$ is a submultiset of
   that of $\mathcal{M}$.
  \end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: def:exponents
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:exponents}
  For $\lambda\in\Bbbk$, define \[   \mathcal{E}^{\lambda/u}:=\Bbbk((u))e_\lambda,   \qquad   \nabla_{\partial_u}e_\lambda   =-\lambda u^{-2}e_\lambda. \] Thus \[   \nabla_{\partial_u}(f e_\lambda)   =(f'-\lambda u^{-2}f)e_\lambda. \] After adjoining an invertible differential symbol $s_\lambda$ satisfying $s_\lambda'=\lambda u^{-2}s_\lambda$, the section $s_\lambda e_\lambda$ is horizontal. We write $s_\lambda=e^{-\lambda/u}$. 
  
  A meromorphic connection $\mathcal{M}$ is said to be of \emph{unramified exponential type} if it decomposes as
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:elementary}
   \mathcal{M}\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
   \mathcal{E}^{\lambda/u}\otimes\mathcal{R}_\lambda
  \end{equation}
  for a finite indexing set $\Lambda\subset\Bbbk$ and a collection of regular-singular connections $\mathcal{R}_\lambda$. 
  
  For a regular-singular connection $\mathcal{R}$, we define its multiset of exponents:
  \[
  \operatorname{Exp}(\mathcal{R}):=\bigl\{\bigl\{ -\vartheta+\mathbb{Z} \bigm| \vartheta\text{ is a residue eigenvalue of } \mathcal{R} \bigr\}\bigr\},
  \]
  where the elements are counted with their algebraic multiplicities. We extend this definition to the elementary factors setting $\operatorname{Exp}(\mathcal{E}^{\lambda/u}\otimes\mathcal{R}_\lambda):=\operatorname{Exp}(\mathcal{R}_\lambda)$.
  
  A regular-singular connection has \emph{rational residue eigenvalues} if the residue eigenvalues of one, equivalently every, logarithmic lattice lie in $\mathbb{Q}$. We abbreviate this condition to \emph{rational residues}. We say that a connection of unramified exponential type, as in \eqref{eq:elementary}, has rational residues if this condition holds for every regular-singular component $\mathcal{R}_\lambda$. Because changing the underlying logarithmic lattice only shifts the residue eigenvalues by integers, Lemma~\ref{lem:lattice-independence} ensures that both the rationality condition and the multiset of exponents $\operatorname{Exp}$ are well-defined and lattice-independent.

label: lem:splitting
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:splitting}
  Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be an $F[[u]]$-lattice in a meromorphic connection $\mathcal{M}$ over $F((u))$ such that $u^2\nabla_{\partial_u}\mathcal{L}\subseteq\mathcal{L}$. Define the leading endomorphism
  \[
  A_0:=(u^2\nabla_{\partial_u})\bmod u\mathcal{L}\in\operatorname{End}_F(\mathcal{L}/u\mathcal{L}),
  \]
  and consider the generalized eigenspace decomposition $\mathcal{L}/u\mathcal{L}=\bigoplus_{\lambda}V_\lambda$, where $V_\lambda$ corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda \in \operatorname{spec}(A_0)$. Then:
  \begin{enumerate}
   \item There exists a unique decomposition $\mathcal{L}=\bigoplus_\lambda\mathcal{L}_\lambda$ into $u^2\nabla_{\partial_u}$-stable $F[[u]]$-submodules such that the reduction modulo $u$ yields $\mathcal{L}_\lambda/u\mathcal{L}_\lambda=V_\lambda$.
   \item This lattice decomposition induces a direct sum decomposition of the meromorphic connection $\mathcal{M}=\bigoplus_\lambda\mathcal{M}_\lambda$, where each $\mathcal{M}_\lambda:=\mathcal{L}_\lambda[u^{-1}]$ is a differential submodule of rank $\operatorname{rk}\mathcal{M}_\lambda=\dim V_\lambda$.
   \item For each eigenvalue $\lambda$, the connection $\mathcal{E}^{\lambda/u}\otimes\mathcal{M}_\lambda$ has a nilpotent leading endomorphism given by $(A_0-\lambda)|_{V_\lambda}$. Consequently, the full connection factors as
   \[
   \mathcal{M}\cong\bigoplus_\lambda\mathcal{E}^{-\lambda/u}\otimes\bigl(\mathcal{E}^{\lambda/u}\otimes\mathcal{M}_\lambda\bigr).
   \]
  \end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: cor:leading-exponential
title: Corollary
body_md: \label{cor:leading-exponential} In the setting of Lemma~\ref{lem:splitting}, suppose that $\mathcal{M}$ is of unramified exponential type: \[   \mathcal{M}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathcal{N}_\lambda,   \qquad   \mathcal{N}_\lambda\cong\mathcal{E}^{\lambda/u}\otimes\mathcal{R}_\lambda, \] where every $\mathcal{R}_\lambda$ is regular singular. Then \[   \Lambda=-\operatorname{spec}(A_0),   \qquad   \mathcal{M}_\lambda=\mathcal{N}_{-\lambda},   \qquad   \operatorname{rk}\mathcal{R}_{-\lambda}=\dim V_\lambda. \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Choose a logarithmic lattice in each $\mathcal{R}_\lambda$. The induced lattice in $\mathcal{N}_\lambda$ has leading endomorphism $-\lambda I$. We first verify that a differential morphism $\phi: \mathcal{M}_{\lambda_1} \to \mathcal{N}_{\lambda_2}$ between two connections with quadratic lattices and disjoint leading spectra is zero, even if the morphism does not preserve the lattices. In chosen lattice bases, write the morphism as a Laurent matrix \[   \phi(u)=u^j\phi_j+u^{j+1}\phi_{j+1}+\cdots,   \qquad \phi_j\neq0. \] If the two connection matrices are $A(u)/u^2$ and $B(u)/u^2$, horizontality gives \[   u^2\phi'(u)+B \phi(u)-\phi(u) A=0. \] The coefficient of $u^j$ is \[   B_0\phi_j-\phi_jA_0=0. \] Disjoint leading spectra make this Sylvester operator invertible, a contradiction. Apply this observation to the components of the identity map between $\mathcal{M}=\bigoplus_{\lambda_1} \mathcal{M}_{\lambda_1}$ and $\mathcal{M}=\bigoplus_{\lambda_2}\mathcal{N}_{\lambda_2}$. Every component vanishes unless $\lambda_1=-\lambda_2$. Applying the same argument in the reverse direction identifies $\mathcal{M}_{\lambda_1}$ with the embedded summand $\mathcal{N}_{-\lambda_1}$. The rank formula follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:splitting}.

label: lem:descent
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:descent}
  Let $F\subseteq F'$ be algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero and
  let $A_1, A_2$ be matrices over $F$. Then $\partial_u+A_2u^{-2}+A_1u^{-1}$ is of
  unramified exponential type with rational residues over $F((u))$ if and only
  if its extension to $F'((u))$ is.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:splitting} over $F$ to the natural lattice.
  Its uniqueness identifies the scalar extensions of its spectral
  summands with those supplied by the same lemma over $F'$.
  For an eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A_2$, set
  $\mathcal{N}_\lambda:=\mathcal{E}^{\lambda/u}\otimes\mathcal{M}_\lambda$.
  By Corollary~\ref{cor:leading-exponential}, unramified exponential
  type is equivalent to regular singularity of every $\mathcal{N}_\lambda$.
  It remains to descend that property and rationality of residues.
  
  Fix $\mathcal{N}:=\mathcal{N}_\lambda$, an $F[[u]]$-lattice $\mathcal L_0$
  with basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, and set $D:=u\nabla_{\partial_u}$.
  If the extended connection is regular singular, choose a
  logarithmic $F'[[u]]$-lattice $\mathcal L'$ in it. Write
  $\mathcal L'_0:=\mathcal L_0\otimes_{F[[u]]}F'[[u]]$.
  Commensurability gives integers $a,b\geq0$ such that
  \[
  u^b\mathcal L'_0\subseteq\mathcal L'
  \subseteq u^{-a}\mathcal L'_0.
  \]
  The shifted lattice $u^{-b}\mathcal L'$ is also $D$-stable,
  contains $\mathcal L'_0$, and lies in
  $u^{-(a+b)}\mathcal L'_0$. Consequently, for every $j\geq0$
  and $1\leq\ell\leq r$,
  \[
  D^je_\ell\in u^{-(a+b)}\mathcal L'_0
  \cap\bigl(\mathcal L_0\otimes_{F[[u]]}F((u))\bigr)
  =u^{-(a+b)}\mathcal L_0.
  \]
  The $F[[u]]$-submodule
  \[
  \mathcal L_\infty:=
  \sum_{j\geq0,\,1\leq\ell\leq r}F[[u]]D^je_\ell
  \]
  is therefore contained in a finite free module. Since $F[[u]]$
  is Noetherian, it is finitely generated; since it contains $\mathcal L_0$ and is torsion-free, it is a full free lattice.
  The Leibniz rule makes it $D$-stable. Thus $\mathcal{N}$ is regular
  singular over $F((u))$. Conversely, a logarithmic lattice
  extends to one over $F'[[u]]$.
  
  The residue of $\mathcal L_\infty$ has entries in $F$.
  After extension, its eigenvalues represent the same classes
  modulo $\mathbb{Z}$ as those of $\mathcal L'$ by
  Lemma~\ref{lem:lattice-independence}. If the latter are rational,
  then each eigenvalue of the former belongs to $\mathbb{Q}$, since it
  differs from a rational number by an integer. The same lemma
  identifies the exponent multiset before and after extension.

label: thm:fano
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:fano}
  Let $X$ be a smooth projective Fano variety and let $b$ be a rational point
  of the one-parameter small locus \eqref{eq:very-small}. Then the formal
  disk connection $\mathcal{H}_b^{\mathrm{mer}}$ is of unramified exponential type
  with rational residues, and
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:fano-decomposition}
   {\widehat \mathcal{H}}_b^{\mathrm{mer}}
   =\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(K_b^{\mathrm F})}\mathcal{E}^{-\lambda/u}\otimes\mathcal{R}_{\lambda,b},
   \qquad
   \operatorname{rk}\mathcal{R}_{\lambda,b}=\operatorname{mult}_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;K_b^{\mathrm F}).
  \end{equation}
  The same assertion holds for a graded ambient subspace
  closed under the small quantum product, with spectrum
  and algebraic multiplicities computed for
  $K_b^{\mathrm F}|_{\mathbf R}$. On the Hodge-fixed part, these formal summands are the completed
  fibers of the local spectral decomposition given by Theorem \ref{thm:hyzz}.

label: thm:chen
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:chen}
  Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed monotone symplectic manifold of real dimension
  $2\nu$, and let $\star_1$ be its small quantum product with the monotone Novikov parameter specialized to $1$. The connection
  \[
  \partial_u-\frac{c_1(TM)\star_1}{u^2}+\frac{\mu}{u},
  \qquad \mu|_{\mathrm{H}^a(M)}=\frac{a-\nu}{2}\,\operatorname{id},
  \]
  on $\mathrm{H}^*(M;\mathbb{C})((u))$ is of unramified exponential type and has
  quasi-unipotent regularized monodromies.
head: environment

label: eq:homogeneity
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\{\sigma_i\}$ be a homogeneous basis, with
  $d_i:=\deg\sigma_i$.
  To obtain the coefficient of $\sigma_i$ in
  $c_1(TX)\star\sigma_j$, pair with a class of degree
  $2n-d_i$. The three-point dimension constraint is
  \[
  2+d_j+(2n-d_i)=2n+2c_1(TX)\cdot\beta.
  \]
  Writing $a:=P\cdot\beta$ gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:homogeneity}
   d_i+2ra=d_j+2.
  \end{equation}
  Thus each nonzero matrix entry of $K_b^{\mathrm F}=-c_1(TX)\star_b$ is
  $\kappa_{ij}q^{a_{ij}}$, with
  $\kappa_{ij}\in\mathbb{Q}$ and
  $a_{ij}=(d_j+2-d_i)/(2r)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}$.
  
  Choose $\alpha\in\Bbbk^\times$ satisfying
  $\alpha^{2r}=q(b)$ and put
  $D:=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha^{d_i})$.
  Then
  \[
  (DK_b^{\mathrm F}D^{-1})_{ij}
  =\kappa_{ij}\alpha^{d_i+2ra_{ij}-d_j}
  =\alpha^2\kappa_{ij},
  \]
  so $DK_b^{\mathrm F}D^{-1}=\alpha^2K_1^{\mathrm F}$, where
  $K_1^{\mathrm F}$ denotes the algebraic specialization at $q=1$.
  Since $D$ and $G$ are diagonal in this basis,
  $DGD^{-1}=G$.
  The constant gauge transforms the connection into
  \[
  \partial_u+\frac{\alpha^2K_1^{\mathrm F}}{u^2}+\frac Gu.
  \]
  With $v=u/\alpha^2$, one has
  $\partial_v=\alpha^2\partial_u$, and hence
  \[
  \nabla_{\partial_v}
  =\alpha^2\nabla_{\partial_u}
  =\partial_v+\frac{K_1^{\mathrm F}}{v^2}+\frac Gv.
  \]
  
  More generally, under $v=cu$,
  \[
  \left(-\frac{\lambda}{u^2}+\frac{\vartheta}{u}\right)du
  =
  \left(-\frac{c\lambda}{v^2}+\frac{\vartheta}{v}\right)dv.
  \]
  Thus exponential parameters are multiplied by $c$,
  whereas residue eigenvalues are unchanged.
  It suffices to treat the algebraic specialization $q=1$ of
  the polynomial connection matrix. This is not a point of the
  non-Archimedean small locus $0<|q|<1$.
  
  Embed $\overline\mathbb{Q}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{C}$ and choose a K\"ahler form representing
  $c_1(TX)$. The resulting symplectic manifold is monotone; its small quantum
  product at Novikov parameter $1$ coincides with the algebraic one
  \cite{Siebert}, and $G$ is the grading operator in Theorem \ref{thm:chen}. By Theorem \ref{thm:chen}, the
  connection is of unramified exponential type with quasi-unipotent regularized
  monodromies. A residue eigenvalue $\vartheta$ gives the monodromy eigenvalue
  $e^{-2\pi i\vartheta}$, which is a root of unity, so $\vartheta\in\mathbb{Q}$. Applying
  Lemma \ref{lem:descent} to $\overline\mathbb{Q}\subset\mathbb{C}$ and then to
  $\overline\mathbb{Q}\subset\Bbbk$, and undoing the rescaling and the gauge, gives the
  claim at $b$.
  
  On the natural lattice $\mathrm{H}^*(X,\Bbbk)[[u]]$,
  the leading endomorphism is $K_b^{\mathrm F}$.
  Corollary~\ref{cor:leading-exponential} therefore
  identifies the exponential parameters with the
  negatives of the eigenvalues of $K_b^{\mathrm F}$ and gives the rank formula
  in \eqref{eq:fano-decomposition}. For a graded ambient subspace preserved by $K_b^{\mathrm F}$, apply
  Lemma~\ref{lem:splitting} to its natural lattice as well.
  The Laurent-matrix argument in the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:leading-exponential} shows that the inclusion
  has no components between distinct leading eigenvalues.
  After the corresponding exponential twists, its summands are
  differential submodules of the $\mathcal{R}_{\lambda,b}$.
  Lemma~\ref{lem:lattice-independence} gives regular singularity
  and rational residue eigenvalues for each of them.
  
  Finally, $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{Hdg}}$ is maximal, so Theorem \ref{thm:hyzz} yields a local product of
  bases and an external sum lifting the generalized eigenspaces of
  $K_b^{\mathrm F}$. Completion at $u=0$ and uniqueness of the formal
  splitting identify the fibers of the factors with the Hodge-fixed summands of
  \eqref{eq:fano-decomposition}.

label: prop:nef
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:nef}
  Let $W$ be a connected smooth projective variety of dimension $d$ with canonical class $K_W$
  nef, and let $b\in B_W^{\mathsf{Hod}}(\Bbbk)$. The disk connection at $b$ has the
  single exponential parameter $y_0(b)$. Moreover, after twisting by $\mathcal{E}^{-y_0(b)/u}$, the connection is
  regular singular with rational residues, and on the Hodge-fixed part
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:nef-exponents}
   \operatorname{rk}\mathcal{R}_{\operatorname{Hdg}}=\dim_\mathbb{Q} H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(W),
   \qquad
   \operatorname{Exp}(\mathcal{R}_{\operatorname{Hdg}})=\{\!\{\overline{d/2}^{\,[\dim H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(W)]}\}\!\},
  \end{equation}
  where the superscript $[m]$ denotes $m$ repetitions.
head: environment

label: eq:degree-nef
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $b'$ be obtained from $b$ by setting $y_0=0$.
  The string equation gives $\star_b=\star_{b'}$; since
  $\partial_{y_0}\mathsf{Eu}=\mathbf1$, it also gives
  $K_b^{\mathrm F}=K_{b'}^{\mathrm F}-y_0(b)\operatorname{id}$. Thus, after tensoring by
  $\mathcal{E}^{-y_0(b)/u}$, we may assume $y_0(b)=0$.
  Consider a nonzero contribution to the product of
  classes of degrees $2p$ and $a$, with curve class
  $\beta$ and additional insertions of degrees
  $2p_1,\ldots,2p_k$.
  If the output has degree $h$, its Poincar\'e-dual test class has degree $2d-h$. The dimension axiom
  therefore gives
  \[
  2p+a+(2d-h)+2\sum_{\nu=1}^k p_\nu
  =2\bigl(d+c_1(TW)\cdot\beta+k\bigr).
  \]
  Solving for $h$ yields
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:degree-nef}
   h=a+2p+2\sum_{\nu=1}^k(p_\nu-1)
   -2c_1(TW)\cdot\beta.
  \end{equation}
  Because $b\in B_W^{\mathsf{Hod}}$, all remaining additive insertions
  are rational Hodge classes. The unit coordinate has been set
  to zero, and all degree-two Hodge directions belong to the
  N\'eron--Severi space and have been absorbed into the
  Novikov variables. Thus $p_\nu\geq2$; every term of $\mathsf{Eu}$ has
  $p\geq1$ since $y_0=0$; and $c_1(TW)\cdot\beta\leq0$. Hence $K^{\mathrm F}=-\mathsf{Eu}\star$
  strictly raises degree, and we write $K^{\mathrm F}=\sum_{j\geq1}K_j^{\mathrm F}$ with $K_j^{\mathrm F}$ raising
  degree by $2j$.
  
  On $\mathrm{H}^{2p+\epsilon}(W,\Bbbk)$, with
  $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$, define $\Gamma:=p\,\operatorname{id}$.
  On the parity-$\epsilon$ part,
  \[
  G=\Gamma+\frac{\epsilon-d}{2}\operatorname{id}.
  \]
  Since $K_j^{\mathrm F}$ raises degree by $2j$,
  \[
  u^\Gamma K_j^{\mathrm F} u^{-\Gamma}=u^jK_j^{\mathrm F}.
  \]
  Moreover, applying both sides to a section gives
  \[
  u^\Gamma\partial_u u^{-\Gamma}
  =\partial_u-\frac{\Gamma}{u}.
  \]
  Consequently,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:nef-gauge}
   u^\Gamma\nabla_{\partial_u}u^{-\Gamma}
   =
   \partial_u+\sum_{j\geq1}u^{j-2}K_j^{\mathrm F}
   +\frac{\epsilon-d}{2u}\operatorname{id}.
  \end{equation}
  Only the term $j=1$ contributes to the residue.
  Thus, the transformed connection is logarithmic,
  with residue:
  \[
  K_1^{\mathrm F}+\frac{\epsilon-d}{2}\operatorname{id}.
  \]
  The operator $K_1^{\mathrm F}$ raises degree by two, so
  $(K_1^{\mathrm F})^{d+1}=0$. Every residue eigenvalue on the
  parity-$\epsilon$ part is therefore
  $(\epsilon-d)/2$, and our convention for exponents
  gives the class $\overline{(d-\epsilon)/2}$.
  
  Equivalently,
  $u^{-\Gamma}\mathrm{H}^*(W,\Bbbk)[[u]]$
  is a logarithmic lattice for the connection after
  the scalar exponential twist.
  Returning to the original point $b$, put
  \[
  \mathcal{R}_{\operatorname{Hdg}}:=
  \mathcal{E}^{-y_0(b)/u}\otimes
  {\widehat \mathcal{H}}_{\operatorname{Hdg},b}^{\mathrm{mer}}.
  \]
  The gauge preserves the Hodge subspace, which is
  purely even. Hence $\mathcal{R}_{\operatorname{Hdg}}$ has rank
  $\dim_\mathbb{Q} H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(W)$ and all its exponents are
  $\overline{d/2}$, as asserted.
  The full connection is
  $\mathcal{E}^{y_0(b)/u}$ tensored with a nonzero regular-singular connection, so its only exponential parameter is $y_0(b)$.

label: lem:cyclic
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cyclic}
  Put $N:=\dim_\mathbb{Q} H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(X)$, and let
  $b\in B_X^{\mathsf{Hod}}(\Bbbk)$. Assume that
  \[
  \mathbf1,\mathsf{Eu}_b,\mathsf{Eu}_b^{\star2},\ldots,\mathsf{Eu}_b^{\star(N-1)}
  \]
  form a basis of $T_bB_X^{\mathsf{Hod}}$.
  Equivalently, the minimal polynomial of
  $K_b^{\mathrm F}|_{H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(X)\otimes_\mathbb{Q}\Bbbk}$ has degree $N$.
  Then there is an admissible neighborhood $U\subset B_X^{\mathsf{Hod}}$
  of $b$ such that:
  \begin{enumerate}
   \item On $\mathcal{H}_{\operatorname{Hdg}}|_{U\times\{0\}}$, the number of distinct
   eigenvalues of $K^{\mathrm F}$, their algebraic multiplicities, and their Jordan block sizes are constant.
   The number of distinct eigenvalues on full cohomology is also
   constant on $U$.
   \item If ${\widehat \mathcal{H}}_b^{\mathrm{mer}}$ is of unramified exponential
   type, then so is ${\widehat \mathcal{H}}_{b'}^{\mathrm{mer}}$ for every
   $b'\in U(\Bbbk)$. After matching the eigenvalues by the local
   spectral decomposition, the corresponding regular-singular
   factors are isomorphic over $\Bbbk((u))$.
  \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In a unital algebra, a polynomial in multiplication by an
  element vanishes when its value on the unit vanishes.
  Since $K_b^{\mathrm F}$ is multiplication by $-\mathsf{Eu}_b$, this proves
  the stated equivalence. The cyclic determinant remains nonzero in a neighborhood of $b$, so these powers give a local frame.
  By \eqref{eq:sign}, the powers of $\mathsf{Eu}^{\mathrm F}=-\mathsf{Eu}$ give
  the same frame. The Euler leaf of the maximal Hodge-invariant
  F-bundle in Theorem~\ref{cl:formal-persistence} is consequently
  a neighborhood of $b$ in $B_X^{\mathsf{Hod}}$.
  Theorem~\ref{cl:formal-persistence} gives local constancy of the spectral multiplicities.
  Cyclicity gives one Jordan block for each eigenvalue, whose size
  is its multiplicity. Lemma~\ref{lem:reduced-spectrum} provides
  the assertion about the full spectrum.
  
  For the formal-type assertion on full cohomology, use
  Remark~\ref{rem:compatible-persistence}. Indeed, for
  $X_p=p_\star(-\mathsf{Eu})$, associativity gives on the full bundle
  \[
  \nabla_{uX_p}|_{u=0}
  =p_\star(-\mathsf{Eu})\star(-)=p(K^{\mathrm F}).
  \]
  Thus, the compatibility required there holds along the Hodge leaf,
  and the same transport preserves all regular-singular factors.

label: lem:scalar-fuchs
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:scalar-fuchs}
  Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a differential module of rank $m$ over $\Bbbk((u))$,
  let $D=\nabla_\delta$, and let $v$ be a cyclic vector, meaning that
  $v,Dv,\ldots,D^{m-1}v$ form a basis over $\Bbbk((u))$, where $m$ is the rank. Write
  \[
  D^mv+\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}a_iD^iv=0,
  \qquad a_i\in\Bbbk((u)).
  \]
  Then $\mathcal{M}$ is regular singular if and only if
  $a_i\in\Bbbk[[u]]$ for every $i$. In this case,
  \[
  \mathcal{L}_v:=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}\Bbbk[[u]]D^iv
  \]
  is a logarithmic lattice, and the characteristic polynomial of its
  residue is
  \[
  T^m+\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}a_i(0)T^i.
  \]

label: prop:cyclic-transport
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:cyclic-transport}
  Suppose that $b\in S^{\mathrm{cyc}}(\Bbbk)$ and that $\mathcal M_b$
  is of unramified exponential type with rational residues.
  Then, for every $s\in S^{\mathrm{cyc}}(\Bbbk)$, the regularization
  $\mathcal R_s$ is regular singular and
  \[
  F_s=F_b\subset\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}.
  \]
  In particular, every nonempty analytic open subset $O\subseteq S$
  contains a point $s\in S^{\mathrm{cyc}}(\Bbbk)$ with these properties.
  Equivalently, if an analytic open subset
  $O_0\subseteq U_W^{\mathrm{gen}}$ has nonempty inverse image in $S$,
  then it contains the image of such a point.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, lift the decomposition
  $\mathcal A_W=\operatorname{im}P_0\oplus\ker P_0$ to the
  formal lattice over $S$. Locally, the successive off-diagonal
  terms of the disk connection are removed by gauges $I+u^jT_j$.
  At each order, the unknown off-diagonal matrix $T_j$ is determined
  by the commutator with $K^{\mathrm F}$, which is invertible on
  homomorphisms between the two blocks because their spectra are
  disjoint. Its inverse has analytic coefficients on $S$.
  This gives a decomposition over $\mathcal{O}_S[[u]]$, unique with the
  prescribed reduction, so the local decompositions glue; this is
  the relative form of Lemma~\ref{lem:splitting}, obtained by the
  argument of \cite[Prop.~3.26]{HYZZ}.
  
  Let $P(u)$ be the projection onto the selected formal summand along
  its complement. Then $P(u)^2=P(u)$ and $P(0)=P_0$.
  After inverting $u$, both summands are preserved by
  $\nabla_\delta$. For $h=h_\lambda+h_{\mathrm{rest}}$, this gives
  \[
  \nabla_\delta(P h)=\nabla_\delta h_\lambda
  =P(\nabla_\delta h),
  \qquad [\nabla_\delta,P]=0.
  \]
  
  Let
  \[
  \widehat\mathcal{H}:=H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(W)\otimes_\mathbb{Q}\mathcal{O}_S[[u]],
  \qquad
  \mathcal{L}:=P(u)\widehat\mathcal{H},
  \qquad
  v:=P(u)\mathbf1.
  \]
  On $\mathcal{L}[u^{-1}]$ consider
  \[
  D:=\nabla_\delta-\lambda u^{-1}\operatorname{id}.
  \]
  This is the operator of the regularized connection in the
  $u$-direction. Since
  $\nabla_\delta=\delta+K^{\mathrm F}/u+G$, the endomorphism induced by $uD$
  on $\mathcal{L}/u\mathcal{L}=\mathcal A$ is $N$.
  
  Put $w_j:=u^jD^jv$. The Leibniz rule gives
  $w_{j+1}=(uD-ju)w_j$. Starting from $w_0=v$, induction yields
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:scaled-cyclic-basis}
   w_j\in\mathcal{L},
   \qquad w_j\bmod u=N^jv_0.
  \end{equation}
  On $S^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, the reductions of
  $w_0,\ldots,w_{m-1}$ form a basis. Therefore, these sections form a
  basis of $\mathcal{L}$ over $\mathcal{O}_{S^{\mathrm{cyc}}}[[u]]$, and
  $v,Dv,\ldots,D^{m-1}v$ form a basis after inverting $u$.
  
  Write
  \[
  w_m=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}h_i(s,u)w_i,
  \qquad h_i(s,u)\in\mathcal{O}(S^{\mathrm{cyc}})[[u]].
  \]
  Dividing by $u^m$ gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:cyclic-relation}
   D^mv+\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}a_i(s,u)D^iv=0,
   \qquad a_i=-u^{i-m}h_i.
  \end{equation}
  In particular,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:finite-fuchs-bounds}
   a_i(s,u)\in
   u^{i-m}\mathcal{O}(S^{\mathrm{cyc}})[[u]].
  \end{equation}
  
  Every coefficient of every $a_i$ extends meromorphically to $S$.
  Indeed, in a local frame of $\mathcal{L}$, Cramer's rule expresses each
  $h_i$ as a ratio with denominator
  $\Delta(u):=\det(w_0,\ldots,w_{m-1})$.
  Its constant term represents the cyclic-determinant section,
  which is nonzero at $b$ and hence not identically zero on the
  connected smooth space $S$.
  The formal inverse of $\Delta(u)$ has coefficients obtained by
  inverting powers of $\Delta(0)$, so these ratios are coefficientwise
  meromorphic. They are independent of the local frame and thus glue.
  
  We first establish regular singularity on a neighborhood of $b$.
  Apply Theorem \ref{thm:hyzz} to the maximal Hodge-invariant F-bundle near
  $\pi_W(b)$. After shrinking, its base is a product
  $\prod_\alpha B_\alpha$, and the F-bundle is the external sum of
  maximal F-bundles on these factors. The selected spectral summand
  is pulled back from a maximal F-bundle of rank $m$ on one factor
  $B_*$, with $\dim B_*=m$.
  
  At the corresponding point $b_*\in B_*$, the residual endomorphism
  is $K^{\mathrm F}|_{\mathcal A}=\lambda\,\operatorname{id}+N$. Its powers span
  the same algebra as the powers of $N$. Cyclicity, therefore, implies that the powers of the Euler vector field of this maximal factor span $T_{B_*,b_*}$. The Euler-generated leaf through $b_*$ is consequently a neighborhood
  of $b_*$ in $B_*$.
  
  The formal-persistence assertion of \cite[Rem.~3.14]{KKPY}, shown in Theorem~\ref{cl:formal-persistence},
  applied to this maximal factor, shows that its fibers remain of
  unramified exponential type near $b_*$ and that their regularized
  formal connections have constant isomorphism class. Pulling back
  along the product projection and choosing the local spectral
  branch through $b$ gives a nonempty analytic neighborhood
  $V\subseteq S^{\mathrm{cyc}}$ on which $\mathcal R_s$ is regular
  singular with exponent multiset $F_b$ for every
  $s\in V(\Bbbk)$.
  
  By Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar-fuchs}, every negative-power coefficient
  of every $a_i$ vanishes at all rational points of $V$.
  These coefficients are analytic on $V$, so the affinoid
  Nullstellensatz, applied locally, makes them zero analytic
  functions. There are only finitely many such coefficients by \eqref{eq:finite-fuchs-bounds}.
  Each extends meromorphically to $S$, and the identity principle
  therefore makes each identically zero. Thus
  \eqref{eq:cyclic-relation} defines a logarithmic lattice at every
  point of $S^{\mathrm{cyc}}(\Bbbk)$.
  
  Put
  \[
  c_i(s):=\text{coefficient of $u^0$ in the Laurent expansion of $a_i(s,u)$},
  \quad
  p_s(T):=T^m+\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}c_i(s)T^i.
  \]
  For $s\in V(\Bbbk)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar-fuchs} identifies
  the roots of $p_s$, counted with multiplicity, with the residue
  eigenvalues of the cyclic logarithmic lattice. If $\alpha$ is
  such a root, then $-\alpha+\mathbb{Z}\in F_b\subset\mathbb{Q}/\mathbb{Z}$.
  Thus $\alpha=q+k$ for some $q\in\mathbb{Q}$ and $k\in\mathbb{Z}$, and in
  particular $\alpha\in\mathbb{Q}$. The coefficients $c_i(s)$, being
  signed elementary symmetric functions of these roots, also
  belong to $\mathbb{Q}$.
  
  Choose an affinoid neighborhood $V'\subseteq V$ of $b$
  on which
  \[
  |c_i(s)-c_i(b)|<1\qquad(0\leq i<m).
  \]
  At every rational point of $V'$, these differences are rational.
  Since the absolute value is trivial on $\mathbb{Q}$, they must vanish.
  The affinoid $V'$ is reduced, and all its rigid points are
  $\Bbbk$-rational. The affinoid Nullstellensatz gives
  $c_i=c_i(b)$ on $V'$. Since $V'$ contains a nonempty analytic
  open neighborhood of $b$, the meromorphic identity principle
  gives $c_i=c_i(b)\quad\text{on }S$. Consequently $p_s=p_b$ on $S^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, and the negative
  roots modulo $\mathbb{Z}$ give $F_s=F_b$.
  
  Finally, $S^{\mathrm{cyc}}$ is dense and open in $S$. Every
  nonempty analytic open subset of $S$ meets $S^{\mathrm{cyc}}$ in a nonempty analytic open subset, which
  contains a $\Bbbk$-rational point.

label: lem:separation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:separation}
  Let $Y$ be a connected smooth complex projective variety,
  let $Z\subset Y$ be a connected smooth closed subvariety of
  codimension $c\geq2$, and let $E$ be an algebraic vector
  bundle of rank $r\geq1$ on $Y$.
  Consider the comparisons
  \[
  \mathcal F_{\operatorname{Bl}_ZY}
  \simeq
  \mathcal F_Y\boxplus
  \underbrace{\mathcal F_Z\boxplus\cdots\boxplus\mathcal F_Z}_{c-1},
  \qquad
  \mathcal F_{\mathbb{P}(E)}
  \simeq
  \underbrace{\mathcal F_Y\boxplus\cdots\boxplus\mathcal F_Y}_{r}
  \]
  on the analytic comparison domains of \cite[Thms.~4.5 and 4.11, \S\S5.2.4--5.2.5]{KKPY}.
  In (a) and (b), assume that the initial generic Hodge factor has a cyclic
  representative at a $\Bbbk$-rational point, of unramified exponential
  type with rational exponents.
  \begin{itemize}
   \item[(a)] A generic Hodge factor on the left can be
   represented in a comparison domain and transferred to a generic
   Hodge factor of one summand on the right.
   
   \item[(b)] A generic Hodge factor of any specified summand on
   the right can be represented in a
   comparison domain and transferred to a generic Hodge factor on
   the left.
   
   \item[(c)] In both cases the resulting factor has a cyclic representative
   at a $\Bbbk$-rational point, is of unramified exponential type with rational
   exponents, and has the same rank and regularized exponent multiset as the initial factor.
  \end{itemize}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the common algebraic image of the universal Hodge group
  on the cohomology representations occurring in the comparison.
  The comparison is equivariant with respect to its analytic group germ. The blowup and projective-bundle cohomology decompositions involve Tate twists, which restrict trivially to this group. Taking fixed bases and invariant subbundles, therefore, gives the displayed comparisons of purely even maximal F-bundles.
  
  The proof shall proceed in three steps. First, we describe how the comparison works on a common generic locus. Then, we transfer the selected generic Hodge factor, proving (a) and (b). Finally, we check that the comparison preserves cyclicity, rank, and the regularized exponent multiset.
  
  \begin{itemize}
   \item[(i)] We first describe a common generic locus in a comparison domain.
   Require each external summand to lie in its own generic spectral
   locus, and require the spectra of different summands to be
   disjoint. The first condition holds on a dense open subset:
   the comparison domain is open in the product of the bases, and
   each generic spectral locus is dense and open.
   
   For the second condition, the unit coordinate of the $j$th
   summand changes its operator by $K_j^{\mathrm F}\longmapsto K_j^{\mathrm F}-t_j\operatorname{id}$. The parameters $t_j$ vary independently in sufficiently small
   product neighborhoods. For each pair of summands, the resultant
   of their translated characteristic polynomials is a nonzero
   polynomial in the translation parameters. Its zero locus, therefore, has empty interior. Avoiding the finitely many such
   zero loci gives a dense open subset with pairwise disjoint spectra.
   
   Let $d_j $ be the maximal number of distinct eigenvalues for
   the $j$th summand. On the open subset just constructed, the
   external sum has $\sum_jd_j$ distinct eigenvalues.
   The identified open subset on the left meets its dense global
   generic locus. Hence, the maximal number on the left is also
   $\sum_jd_j$: it equals that number at a point of this
   intersection. Thus, the comparison identifies the reduced
   generic spectral covers on a common nonempty open domain.
   On the external-sum side, the cover is the disjoint union of
   the pulled-back covers of the individual summands.
   
   The component-surjectivity results of
   \cite[(5.15) and \S5.2.5]{KKPY} ensure that
   every selected global generic spectral component has a
   representative in the comparison domains. For a component on
   the external-sum side, the corresponding assertion applies to
   each specified copy of a summand. The restrictions just imposed
   remove only loci with empty interiors, so representatives remain
   on the common generic locus.
   
   \item[(ii)] We now transfer the selected generic Hodge factor. Suppose first that the initial factor is on the left.
   Its cyclic locus is nonempty by hypothesis; hence, it is dense and open.
   Proposition~\ref{prop:cyclic-transport} allows us to choose a
   rational representative on the common generic locus at which
   the factor has its original regularized exponent multiset.
   Since the external spectra are disjoint, the transferred
   factor belongs to one summand.
   
   For the converse, start with the selected component of the
   specified external summand. In the product comparison domain,
   the projection to that summand's base is open. The inverse
   image of its dense cyclic locus therefore meets the common
   generic locus in a nonempty open subset of the corresponding
   spectral component. Choose a rational point there and apply
   Proposition~\ref{prop:cyclic-transport} on the selected summand
   before transferring the factor to the left.
   
   \item[(iii)] Let $\Psi(u)$ be the comparison isomorphism.
   It fixes $u$, is regular and invertible at $u=0$, and intertwines
   the connections. Taking the leading coefficient gives $\Psi(0)K_{\mathrm{left}}^{\mathrm F}=K_{\mathrm{right}}^{\mathrm F}\Psi(0)$. Thus, the selected eigenvalue, rank, and leading Jordan form
   are preserved. Twisting both selected factors by
   $\mathcal E^{\lambda/u}$ gives isomorphic regular singular
   connections, so their exponent multisets agree.
   
   Finally, a single Jordan block on the target summand is cyclic
   with respect to that summand's unit by the regular-representation
   argument preceding \eqref{eq:cyclic-locus}. Hence, the transferred
   factor satisfies all the hypotheses of
   Proposition~\ref{prop:cyclic-transport}.
  \end{itemize}

label: prop:low-dimension
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
All transfers in this proof use Lemma~\ref{lem:separation};
  in particular, they preserve rank, cyclicity, and the
  regularized exponent multiset.
  
  For a point, $H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}=\mathbb{Q}\mathbf1$, $G=0$, and $K^{\mathrm F}=-y_0\operatorname{id}$.
  Its regularized connection is trivial, so it has point type.
  Since $\mathbb{P}^a$ is a projective bundle over a point, the
  projective-bundle comparison proves the assertion for every
  projective space.
  
  Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g\geq1$.
  Every genus-zero stable map to $C$ is constant. On the
  Hodge-fixed base, the only additive coordinate is the unit
  coordinate, and the quantum product is the cup product.
  Writing $\eta\in H^2(C,\mathbb{Q})$ for the class with
  $\int_C\eta=1$, we have
  \[
  H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(C)=\mathbb{Q}\mathbf1\oplus\mathbb{Q}\eta,
  \qquad
  K^{\mathrm F}+y_0\operatorname{id}=(2g-2)\,\eta\cup(-).
  \]
  For $g=1$ this is zero, so the rank-two generalized
  eigenspace is never cyclic. For $g\geq2$ it is a single
  nilpotent Jordan block of size two. Proposition~\ref{prop:nef}
  gives the exponent multiset
  $\{\!\{\overline{1/2},\overline{1/2}\}\!\}$. This proves the assertion for curves.
  
  Now let $W$ be a smooth projective surface. Contract its
  $(-1)$-curves to obtain a minimal smooth projective surface
  $\Sigma$. At each step, the selected factor either transfers
  to $\Sigma$ or to a point. In the latter case, it has point type.
  By the classification of minimal smooth projective surfaces
  \cite{BeauvilleSurfaces}, if the minimal surface is rational or ruled, it is either
  $\mathbb{P}^2$ or a projective bundle over a smooth projective curve.
  The preceding cases and the projective-bundle comparison
  then apply.
  
  In the remaining case, $K_\Sigma$ is nef. By
  Proposition~\ref{prop:nef}, the entire Hodge-invariant fiber
  has a single eigenvalue, and its rank is
  \[
  m=\dim H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(\Sigma)=\rho(\Sigma)+2.
  \]
  At a cyclic representative, subtract the unit eigenvalue and
  write $N:=K^{\mathrm F}+y_0\operatorname{id}$. The degree argument in
  Proposition~\ref{prop:nef} shows that $N$ strictly raises
  cohomological degree. Since the Hodge-invariant degrees are
  $0,2,4$, we have $N^3=0$. A single Jordan block of size $m$
  therefore has $m\leq3$. Projectivity implies
  $\rho(\Sigma)\geq1$, so $m=3$ and $\rho(\Sigma)=1$.
  
  Proposition~\ref{prop:nef} then gives
  $F=\{\!\{\overline{0},\overline{0},\overline{0}\}\!\}$.

label: thm:criterion
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:criterion}
  Let $X$ be a connected smooth complex projective variety of
  dimension $2\leq n\leq4$. Suppose that a generic Hodge factor
  has a cyclic representative of unramified exponential type
  with rational residues. Let $m$ be its rank and $F$ its
  regularized exponent multiset. If $X$ is rational, then:
  \begin{enumerate}
   \item if $n=2$, then
   \[
   (m,F)=(1,\{\!\{\overline{0}\}\!\});
   \]
   \item if $n=3$, then
   \[
   (m, F)\in
   \left\{
   (1,\{\!\{\overline{0}\}\!\}),
   (2,\{\!\{\overline{1/2},\overline{1/2}\}\!\})
   \right\};
   \]
   \item if $n=4$, then
   \[
   (m, F)\in
   \left\{
   (1,\{\!\{\overline{0}\}\!\}),
   (2,\{\!\{\overline{1/2},\overline{1/2}\}\!\}),
   (3,\{\!\{\overline{0},\overline{0},\overline{0}\}\!\})
   \right\}.
   \]
  \end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume that $X$ is rational. By weak factorization
  \cite[Thm.~0.1.1]{AKMW}, a
  birational map $X\dashrightarrow\mathbb{P}^n$ factors into a finite
  sequence of blowups and blowdowns between smooth projective
  $n$-folds, with smooth centers of codimension at least two.
  
  Track the selected generic Hodge factor along this sequence.
  If the next variety is the blowup of the current one, use
  the converse direction of Lemma~\ref{lem:separation}, with
  the current variety as the specified summand. If the current
  variety is the blowup of the next one, use the forward
  direction of the lemma. The factor then transfers either
  to the next variety or to one of the copies of the center.
  At every step, its rank, cyclicity, unramified exponential
  type, rational residue eigenvalues, and exponent multiset
  are preserved.
  
  The process terminates either with a factor on a center
  of dimension at most $n-2$, or with a factor on $\mathbb{P}^n$.
  In the latter case Proposition~\ref{prop:low-dimension}
  gives point type. In the former case, the same proposition
  gives point type when $n=2$, point or curve type when
  $n=3$, and point, curve, or surface type when $n=4$.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Substituting the formal series into \eqref{eq:phi-system} and equating the coefficients of $u^s$ yields the primary relation $(\lambda\operatorname{id}-K^{\mathrm F})v_0=0$. Evaluating the coefficients at order $u^{s+k}$ gives the equality
 $(\lambda\operatorname{id}-K^{\mathrm F})v_k=(G+(s+k-1)\operatorname{id})v_{k-1}$. Applying the left kernel vector $w^\top$ annihilates the left-hand side, yielding the stated solvability condition.

 Regarding the final assertion, the formal spectral decomposition provided by
 Theorem~\ref{thm:fano}, after twisting by $\mathcal{E}^{\lambda/u}$, reads
 \[
 \mathcal{R}_\lambda\ \oplus\!
 \bigoplus_{\nu\ne\lambda}
 \mathcal{E}^{(\lambda-\nu)/u}\otimes\mathcal{R}_\nu.
 \]
 Consequently, $\mathcal{R}_\lambda$ operates as a direct summand of the twisted
 matrix connection: the formal isomorphism maps a vector in
 this initial summand to the original cohomology basis via a
 Laurent-series change of basis. For each residue eigenvalue of $\mathcal{R}_\lambda$,
 the constant-residue formal normal form of
 \cite[Prop.~3.12]{PutSinger} (valid over the algebraically
 closed characteristic-zero field $\Bbbk$ by
 \cite[Rem.~3.20(1)]{PutSinger}) yields an
 eigenvector solution carrying the opposite power of $u$ entirely free of
 logarithms. Expressing this solution in the original basis through the
 formal meromorphic isomorphism and the inclusion of the direct
 summand produces a solution to \eqref{eq:phi-system}. Since a Laurent-series change of basis modifies the leading power by an integer,
 its class modulo $\mathbb{Z}$ is the same.

label: ex:cubic3
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:cubic3}
 Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^4$ be a smooth cubic threefold and
 $H=c_1(\mathcal{O}_X(1))$. Lefschetz hyperplane theorem and Poincar\'e duality give
 \[
 H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(X)=\operatorname{span}_\mathbb{Q}\{\mathbf 1,H,H^2,H^3\}.
 \]
 The primitive middle cohomology has odd degree and contributes
 no rational $(p,p)$ classes. Since $X$ has Fano index two, $K^{\mathrm F}=-2H\star(-)$.
 The operator for small quantum multiplication by $H$ is extracted from
 \cite{Givental}; compare
 \cite[\S3]{cai2026cubicthreefoldsymplecticallyirrational}:
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:cubic-matrix}
  K^{\mathrm F}=-\begin{pmatrix}
   0&12q&0&72q^2\\
   2&0&30q&0\\
   0&2&0&12q\\
   0&0&2&0
  \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  G=\operatorname{diag}\Bigl(-\frac32,-\frac12,\frac12,\frac32\Bigr).
 \end{equation}
 The characteristic polynomial and the cyclic determinant evaluate to
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:cubic-spectrum}
  \det(x\operatorname{id}-K^{\mathrm F})=x^2(x^2-108q),
  \qquad
  \det\bigl(\mathbf1,K^{\mathrm F}\mathbf1,(K^{\mathrm F})^2\mathbf1,(K^{\mathrm F})^3\mathbf1\bigr)=64.
 \end{equation}
Thus, the small locus point is generic, and the eigenvalue $\lambda=0$ yields a cyclic generic Hodge factor of rank two.
 We compute the regularized exponents of this factor.
 
 For $\lambda=0$, the right and left kernels of $-K^{\mathrm F}$
 are generated respectively by
 \[
 v_0=(0,-6q,0,1)^\top,\qquad
 w^\top=(1,0,-6q,0).
 \]
 The $k=1$ obstruction in \eqref{eq:application-left-obstruction}
 vanishes identically. Solving the inhomogeneous equation at that order provides
 the particular and general solutions:
 \[
 v_1^{\mathrm{part}}
 =\left(-\frac{q(42s+39)}4,0,\frac{2s+3}4,0\right)^\top,
 \qquad v_1=v_1^{\mathrm{part}}+c v_0.
 \]
 Substituting this general solution into the subsequent obstruction yields an expression strictly independent of the free kernel parameter $c$:
 \[
 w^\top\bigl(G+(s+1)\operatorname{id}\bigr)v_1
 =-\frac{3q}{8}(6s+1)(6s+5).
 \]
 Thus, every exponent class must be represented by one of the
 leading powers $s=-5/6,-1/6$. To verify the two occur, write
 $\phi=(\phi_0,\phi_1,\phi_2,\phi_3)^\top$ and set
 $f=\phi_3$. The last three rows of \eqref{eq:phi-system}
 read
 \[
 \begin{split}
  u(u\partial_u+3/2)f&=2\phi_2,\\
  u(u\partial_u+1/2)\phi_2&=2\phi_1+12qf,\\
  u(u\partial_u-1/2)\phi_1&=2\phi_0+30q\phi_2.
 \end{split}
 \]
 Solving these equations consecutively yields
 \[
 \phi_3=f,\qquad
 \phi_2=\frac u2\Bigl(u\partial_u+\frac32\Bigr)f,\qquad
 \phi_1=\Bigl[\frac{u^2}{4}
 \Bigl(u\partial_u+\frac32\Bigr)^2-6q\Bigr]f,
 \]
 \[
 \phi_0=\Bigl[\frac{u^3}{8}\Bigl(u\partial_u+\frac32\Bigr)^3
 -\frac{qu}{4}(42u\partial_u+39)\Bigr]f.
 \]
 The first row consequently reduces to the scalar differential equation
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:cubic-scalar}
  \Bigl[u^2\Bigl(u\partial_u+\frac32\Bigr)^4
  -3q(6u\partial_u+1)(6u\partial_u+5)\Bigr]f=0.
 \end{equation}
 Conversely, the displayed formulas reconstruct a full horizontal section of
 all four rows from any solution of this scalar equation. Substituting the formal ansatz
 $f=u^s\sum_{k\geq0}a_ku^k$, with $a_0=1$ and
 $a_{-1}=a_{-2}=0$, yields the coefficient recurrence:
 \[
 3q\bigl(6(s+k)+1\bigr)\bigl(6(s+k)+5\bigr)a_k
 =\bigl(s+k-\tfrac12\bigr)^4a_{k-2}.
 \]
 At $k=0$, this confirms the indicial roots $s=-5/6$ and $s=-1/6$. 
                                                                                                 
                                               
                                         
                                        
     
                    
                                                 
                    
                                           
     
 These two admissible leading powers yield two linearly independent log-free solutions, yielding:
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:cubic-exponents}
  m=2,\qquad
  F=\{\!\{\overline{-5/6},\overline{-1/6}\}\!\}
  =\{\!\{\overline{1/6},\overline{5/6}\}\!\}.
 \end{equation}
 This rank-two factor is not of curve type. Theorem~\ref{thm:criterion} therefore
 implies that every smooth cubic threefold is irrational.

body_md:
\label{ex:GM3}
 Let $X\subset\operatorname{Gr}(2,5)$ be the smooth zero locus of a
 section of $\mathcal{O}(1)^{\oplus2}\oplus\mathcal{O}(2)$, and let
 $H=c_1(\mathcal{O}_X(1))$. Adjunction gives $c_1(TX)=H$.
 Using Lefschetz hyperplane theorem and Poincar\'e duality we have
 \[
 H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(X)=\operatorname{span}_\mathbb{Q}\{\mathbf 1,H,H^2,H^3\}.
 \]
 In the ordered basis $\{\mathbf1,H,H^2,H^3\}$, the operator for small quantum multiplication by $H$ is extracted from \cite[Thm.~6.1.1]{Przyjalkowski}; see also \cite{alexeev2026atomicdecompositioncompleteintersection}:
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:gm-matrix}
  K^{\mathrm F}=-\begin{pmatrix}
   0&156q^2&3600q^3&33120q^4\\
   1&10q&380q^2&3600q^3\\
   0&1&10q&156q^2\\
   0&0&1&0
  \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  G=\operatorname{diag}\Bigl(-\frac32,-\frac12,\frac12,\frac32\Bigr).
 \end{equation}
 The characteristic polynomial and the cyclic determinant evaluate to
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:gm-spectrum}
  \det(x\operatorname{id}-K^{\mathrm F})=(x-6q)^2(x^2+32qx-244q^2),
  \qquad
  \det\bigl(\mathbf1,K^{\mathrm F}\mathbf1,(K^{\mathrm F})^2\mathbf1,(K^{\mathrm F})^3\mathbf1\bigr)
  =1.
 \end{equation}
 Since $q\ne0$, the remaining two eigenvalues are distinct from each
 other and from $6q$. The small locus point is therefore generic, and the
 eigenvalue $\lambda=6q$ provides a cyclic generic Hodge factor of rank two.
 
 For $\lambda=6q$, the right and left kernels of
 $6q\operatorname{id}-K^{\mathrm F}$ are generated respectively by
 \[
 v_0=(-360q^3,-60q^2,-6q,1)^\top,
 \qquad
 w^\top=(1,-6q,-60q^2,-360q^3).
 \]
 The initial obstruction $w^\top(G+s\operatorname{id})v_0$ vanishes
 identically. Solving the inhomogeneous equation at order $k=1$ gives
 \[
 v_1=(-q^2(88s+108),-q(22s+27),s+3/2,0)^\top+c v_0.
 \]
 Substituting this general solution into the subsequent obstruction yields an expression independent of the free kernel parameter $c$:
 \[
 w^\top\bigl(G+(s+1)\operatorname{id}\bigr)v_1
 =-16q^2s(s+1).
 \]
 Because $q\ne0$, every log-free leading power is constrained to $s\in\{0,-1\}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:application-matrix-recursion}
 ensures that such a power represents each exponent class of the regular-singular factor. Both admissible powers belong to the class
 $\overline{0}$, and the formal factor has rank two. Therefore, the invariants are
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:gm-exponents}
   m=2,\qquad F=\{\!\{\overline{0},\overline{0}\}\!\}.
 \end{equation}
 This rank-two factor is not of curve type. Theorem~\ref{thm:criterion} therefore implies the irrationality of every smooth ordinary Gushel--Mukai threefold.

body_md:
\label{ex:quartic4}
  Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^5$ be a smooth quartic fourfold and
  $H=c_1(\mathcal{O}_X(1))$. Set
  \[
  \mathbf R=\operatorname{span}_\mathbb{Q}\{\mathbf 1,H,H^2,H^3,H^4\}.
  \]
  Assume that:
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:quartic-hodge-condition}
   \mathrm{H}^4(X,\mathbb{Q})_{\mathrm{prim}}\cap H^{2,2}(X)=0.
  \end{equation}
  View quartics as hyperplane sections of the fourth Veronese embedding
  of $\mathbb{P}^5$. Since $h^{3,1}(\mathbb{P}^5)=0<21=h^{3,1}(X)$,
  \cite[Prop.~3.1]{BFGMP2026} implies this condition for a very general
  quartic fourfold; see also
  \cite[Ex.~6.7]{alexeev2026atomicdecompositioncompleteintersection}. In this case, using
  Lefschetz hyperplane theorem in combination with Poincar\'e duality gives $H_{\operatorname{Hdg}}(X)=\mathbf R$.
  
The matrix of small quantum multiplication is obtained from \cite[Ex.~6.7]{alexeev2026atomicdecompositioncompleteintersection}:
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:quartic-matrix}
   K^{\mathrm F}=-\begin{pmatrix}
    0&48q&0&5568q^2&0\\
    2&0&208q&0&5568q^2\\
    0&2&0&208q&0\\
    0&0&2&0&48q\\
    0&0&0&2&0
   \end{pmatrix},
   \qquad
   G=\operatorname{diag}(-2,-1,0,1,2).
  \end{equation}
  Here $K^{\mathrm F}=-2H\star$, since the Fano index is two. Moreover,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:quartic-spectrum}
   \det(x\operatorname{id}-K^{\mathrm F})=x^3(x^2-1024q),
   \qquad
   \det\bigl(\mathbf1,K^{\mathrm F}\mathbf1,\ldots,(K^{\mathrm F})^4\mathbf1\bigr)=2^{10}.
  \end{equation}
  Under \eqref{eq:quartic-hodge-condition}, this proves cyclicity
  on the entire Hodge-invariant space. Lemma~\ref{lem:cyclic}
  then shows that the small locus point is generic: the Euler powers
  span the five-dimensional Hodge-fixed tangent space, so their leaf
  contains a neighborhood in which the spectral multiplicities are
  constant, and this neighborhood meets the dense generic locus.
  We select the zero eigenvalue, whose single Jordan block on the
  Hodge-invariant space has size three.
  
  For $\lambda=0$, right and left kernels of $-K^{\mathrm F}$
  are generated by
  \[
  v_0=(-288q^2,0,-24q,0,1)^\top,
  \qquad w^\top=(1,0,-24q,0,-288q^2).
  \]
  The obstructions at $k=1$ and $k=2$ vanish identically. Setting
  the free kernel parameters to zero gives particular solutions
  \[
  \begin{split}
   v_1^{\mathrm{part}}
   &=(0,-q(64s+104),0,s/2+1,0)^\top,\\
   v_2^{\mathrm{part}}
   &=(-2q(29s^2+78s+52),0,s^2/4+s+1,0,0)^\top.
  \end{split}
  \]
  More precisely, the general solutions at these orders are
  \[
  \begin{split}
   v_1&=v_1^{\mathrm{part}}+cv_0,\\
   v_2&=v_2^{\mathrm{part}}
   +c(0,-8q(8s+21),0,(s+3)/2,0)^\top+dv_0.
  \end{split}
  \]
  Keeping both parameters in the $k=3$ solvability condition,
  they cancel and leave
  \[
  w^\top\bigl(G+(s+2)\operatorname{id}\bigr)v_2
  =-16q(s+1)(2s+1)(2s+3).
  \]
  This restricts the possible leading powers to
  $-3/2,-1,-1/2$.

  \begin{equation}\label{eq:quartic-exponents}
   m=3,\qquad
   F=\{\!\{\overline{-3/2},\overline{-1},\overline{-1/2}\}\!\}
   =\{\!\{\overline{0},\overline{1/2},\overline{1/2}\}\!\}.
  \end{equation}
  This rank-three factor is not of surface type, so Theorem~\ref{thm:criterion} implies
  irrationality. In particular, every smooth quartic fourfold satisfying \eqref{eq:quartic-hodge-condition} is irrational, and hence every very general smooth quartic fourfold is irrational.

label: prop:product
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:product}
  Let $V$ be a connected smooth complex projective threefold.
  Suppose it has a cyclic generic Hodge factor of rank two, of
  unramified exponential type with rational residues, whose exponent
  multiset $F$ is different from
  $\{\!\{\overline{1/2},\overline{1/2}\}\!\}$. Then $V\times\mathbb{P}^1$ is irrational.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write
  \[
  V\times\mathbb{P}^1\cong\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{O}_V\oplus\mathcal{O}_V).
  \]
  The projective-bundle comparison of Lemma~\ref{lem:separation}
  identifies the Hodge-invariant F-bundle of this product, on a
  comparison domain, with the external sum of two copies of
  $\mathcal F_V$. The converse direction of the same lemma transfers
  the selected factor of either specified copy to a cyclic generic
  Hodge factor on $V\times\mathbb{P}^1$, preserving its rank and exponent
  multiset.
  For a rational fourfold, Theorem~\ref{thm:criterion} allows only
  curve type among rank-two cyclic generic Hodge factors. The
  transferred factor violates this condition, proving irrationality.

label: lem:app-transport-operators
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:app-transport-operators}
  Let $(\mathcal{H},\nabla)/B$ be an F-bundle, let $p\in\Bbbk[z]$,
  and let $X_p$ be an even analytic vector field on $B$ satisfying
  $\mu(X_p)=p(K^{\mathrm F})$. On $\widehat\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{mer}}$, set
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-transport-operators}
   x:=\nabla_{u^2\partial_u},\qquad
   \partial_x:=u^{-1},\qquad
   \widehat\nabla_p:=\nabla_{X_p}-p(x)\partial_x.
  \end{equation}
  Here $u$ and $\partial_x$ act by multiplication, and products of operators denote composition, with the rightmost operator
  acting first. Then $x$ and $\widehat\nabla_p$ preserve every
  shifted lattice $u^a\widehat\mathcal{H}$, $a\in\mathbb{Z}$. Moreover, $x_{|\widehat\mathcal{H}}\bmod u=K^{\mathrm F}$, and
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-transport-commutators}
   [\widehat\nabla_p,x]=-p(x),\qquad
   [\widehat\nabla_p,\partial_x]=p'(x)\partial_x,\qquad
   [\widehat\nabla_p,u]=-up'(x).
  \end{equation}
head: environment

label: eq:app-x-shift
title: Proof
body_md:
By the defining pole condition of an F-bundle, $x$ preserves
  $\widehat\mathcal{H}$ and reduces to $K^{\mathrm F}$ modulo $u$.
  The Leibniz rule gives, for every $a\in\mathbb{Z}$,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-x-shift}
   x(u^av)=u^a x(v)+a u^{a+1}v,
   \qquad v\in\widehat\mathcal{H}^{\mathrm{mer}}.
  \end{equation}
  Thus $x$, and hence every polynomial in $x$, preserves all
  the shifted lattices. Taking $a=-1$ in
  \eqref{eq:app-x-shift} yields $[\partial_x,x]=\operatorname{id}$. Consequently,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-polynomial-commutators}
   [\partial_x,p(x)]=p'(x),\qquad
   [p(x),u]=up'(x)u.
  \end{equation}
  The second identity follows from the first by commuting
  $p(x)$ with $u\partial_x=\operatorname{id}$.
  
  We next check that $\widehat\nabla_p$ preserves
  $\widehat\mathcal{H}$. Both $u\nabla_{X_p}$ and $p(x)$ preserve
  this lattice, and their reductions are equal:
  \[
  (u\nabla_{X_p})\bmod u=\mu(X_p)
  =p(K^{\mathrm F})=p(x)\bmod u.
  \]
  Their difference, therefore, has image in $u\widehat\mathcal{H}$.
  Moving $\partial_x=u^{-1}$ to the left in
  \eqref{eq:app-transport-operators}, using
  \eqref{eq:app-polynomial-commutators}, gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-lattice-transport}
   \widehat\nabla_p
   =u^{-1}\bigl(u\nabla_{X_p}-p(x)\bigr)+p'(x).
  \end{equation}
  Each term on the right preserves $\widehat\mathcal{H}$.
  
  Since $X_p$ is a vector field on $B$, it is independent of
  $u$. Flatness and the Leibniz rule give
  $[\nabla_{X_p},x]=[\nabla_{X_p},\partial_x]=0$.
  Using \eqref{eq:app-polynomial-commutators}, we obtain
  \[
  \begin{aligned}
  [\widehat\nabla_p,x]
  &=-[p(x)\partial_x,x]=-p(x),\\
  [\widehat\nabla_p,\partial_x]
  &=-[p(x),\partial_x]\partial_x=p'(x)\partial_x.
  \end{aligned}
  \]
  Commuting $\widehat\nabla_p$ with $u\partial_x=\operatorname{id}$
  then gives $[\widehat\nabla_p,u]=-up'(x)$, proving
  \eqref{eq:app-transport-commutators}.
  Finally, these identities can be written as
  \[
  \widehat\nabla_p u=u\bigl(\widehat\nabla_p-p'(x)\bigr),
  \qquad
  \widehat\nabla_p u^{-1}
  =u^{-1}\widehat\nabla_p+p'(x)u^{-1}.
  \]
  Starting with $\widehat\mathcal{H}$ and using that $p'(x)$
  preserves every shifted lattice, induction in both directions
  proves the assertion for $u^a\widehat\mathcal{H}$.

label: lem:key
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:app-bracket-reduction
title: Proof
body_md:
Rearranging \eqref{eq:app-lattice-transport} gives
  \[
  u\nabla_{X_p}=p(x)+u\bigl(\widehat\nabla_p-p'(x)\bigr).
  \]
  All operators in parentheses preserve the $u$-adic filtration.
  Moreover, $[p(x),u]$ has image in $u^2\widehat\mathcal{H}$ by
  \eqref{eq:app-polynomial-commutators}. Expanding the
  commutator and discarding terms with image in
  $u^2\widehat\mathcal{H}$ therefore gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-bracket-reduction}
  \begin{aligned}
  [u\nabla_{X_p},u\nabla_{X_q}]
  &\equiv u\bigl([p(x),\widehat\nabla_q]
  +[\widehat\nabla_p,q(x)]\bigr)\\
  &=u\bigl(p'(x)q(x)-p(x)q'(x)\bigr)
  \pmod{u^2\widehat\mathcal{H}}.
  \end{aligned}
  \end{equation}
  For the equality, use the first commutator in
  \eqref{eq:app-transport-commutators} and  Leibniz rule. On the other hand, flatness gives
  \[
  [u\nabla_{X_p},u\nabla_{X_q}]=u^2\nabla_{[X_p,X_q]}.
  \]
  Dividing \eqref{eq:app-bracket-reduction} by $u$ and reducing
  modulo $u$ proves \eqref{eq:key}. The injectivity of $\mu$ and Equation~\eqref{eq:F-Euler-powers} give \eqref{eq:involution}.

label: cl:formal-persistence
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first construct $W$ and prove the spectral assertion.
  We then construct parallel transport for
  $\widehat\nabla_p$ along a flow of $X_p$ and show that it
  preserves the regular-singular factors.
  
  \medskip
  \noindent\emph{Construction of the integral germ.}
  Let $n=\dim B$. By the Cayley--Hamilton theorem and
  \eqref{eq:F-Euler-powers}, the fields
  $X_1,X_z,\ldots,X_{z^{n-1}}$ generate the distribution
  \eqref{eq:app-euler-distribution} over $\mathcal{O}_B$.
  Equation~\eqref{eq:involution} shows that it is involutive.
  Its rank need not be constant in a neighborhood in $B$, so
  we construct its integral germ using flows.
  
  The local analytic flows of the fields $X_p$ exist by
  \cite[Lem.~3.6]{HYZZ}. For each such flow,
  \eqref{eq:involution}, followed by the Cayley--Hamilton theorem,
  gives a finite linear differential system for the pullbacks
  of the generators. Thus, the flow preserves $\mathcal D$ and
  its rank. Choose $r=\dim\mathcal D_b$ of the generators
  whose values at $b$ are independent. Their successive flows
  define an analytic map from an $r$-dimensional polydisk to
  $B$, with injective differential at the origin. After
  shrinking, its image is a closed embedded smooth germ $W$.
  Flow invariance gives $\dim\mathcal D_w=r$ on this image,
  and the differential of the parametrization has image
  $\mathcal D_w$. Hence $T_wW=\mathcal D_w$.
  Uniqueness follows because any other integral germ through $b$ has dimension $r$ and is preserved by the same flows, thus agreeing as a germ. This proves (i).
  
  \medskip
  \noindent\emph{Spectral constancy on $T_W$.}
  Write $L:=\mathsf{Eu}^{\mathrm F}\circ(-)|_{T_W}$; it preserves
  $T_W$ because $LX_q=X_{zq}$. Equation~\eqref{eq:involution}
  gives
  \[
  (\mathrm{Lie}_{X_p}L)(X_q)
  =[X_p,X_{zq}]-L[X_p,X_q]=-X_{pq}.
  \]
  Since the fields $X_q$ span $T_W$, this is the identity
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:Lie-derivative-equality}
   \mathrm{Lie}_{X_p}L=-p(L).
  \end{equation}
  Let $\Phi_s$ be the local flow of $X_p$, and let
  $\varphi_s$ be the scalar analytic flow determined by
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-scalar-flow}
   \partial_s\varphi_s(z)=-p(\varphi_s(z)),\qquad
   \varphi_0(z)=z.
  \end{equation}
  Thus \eqref{eq:Lie-derivative-equality} gives
  $\Phi_s^*L=\varphi_s(L)$. For small $s$, the function
  $\varphi_s$ is injective on the finite set $\operatorname{spec}(L_b)$
  and $\varphi_s'(\lambda)\ne0$ at each of its elements.
  On a generalized $\lambda$-eigenspace, write
  $L_b=\lambda\operatorname{id}+N$, where $N$ is nilpotent. Taylor expansion
  gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-jordan-transport}
   \varphi_s(\lambda\operatorname{id}+N)-\varphi_s(\lambda)\operatorname{id}
   =N g_s(N),\qquad g_s(0)=\varphi_s'(\lambda)\ne0.
  \end{equation}
  The operator $g_s(N)$ is invertible and commutes with $N$.
  Consequently, \eqref{eq:app-jordan-transport} has the same
  kernels of powers as $N$. The eigenvalue multiplicities, and
  indeed the Jordan block sizes, are therefore unchanged along
  each generating flow. Composing these flows proves (ii).
  
  \medskip
  \noindent\emph{Parallel transport on the completed lattices.}
  Fix a polynomial $p$ and a flow curve $b_s=\Phi_s(b)$.
  We use the operators $x$, $\partial_x$, and
  $\widehat\nabla_p$ of \eqref{eq:app-transport-operators}.
  In an analytic trivialization along this curve, write
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-analytic-operators}
   x=u^2\partial_u+C(s,u),\qquad
   \nabla_{X_p}=\partial_s+u^{-1}B(s,u),\qquad
   B(s,0)=p(C(s,0)),
  \end{equation}
  where $B$ and $C$ are analytic matrices. Put
  $\delta:=u\partial_u$, so that $x=u\delta+C(s,u)$.
  When $p(u\delta+C(s,u))$ is written with all powers of
  $\delta$ on the right, its constant term modulo $u$ is
  $p(C(s,0))$, and all its positive-degree coefficients are
  divisible by $u$. Equation~\eqref{eq:app-lattice-transport}
  therefore takes the form
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-bounded-transport}
   \widehat\nabla_p=\partial_s+A(s,u,\delta),
  \end{equation}
  with $A$ polynomial in $\delta$ and analytic in $(s,u)$.
  
  On a sufficiently small closed $u$-disk, $\delta$ is bounded
  in the Gauss norm, with $\|\delta\|\leq1$. Thus $A$ defines
  an analytic family of bounded operators. Write
  $A(s)=\sum_{j\geq0}A_js^j$, and choose $M\geq1$ such that
  $\|A_j\|\leq M^{j+1}$. Parallel transport is obtained by
  solving
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-transport-recursion}
  \begin{gathered}
  (\partial_s+A(s))T_s=0,\qquad T_0=\operatorname{id},\\
  T_s=\sum_{n\geq0}T_ns^n,\qquad
  (n+1)T_{n+1}=-\sum_{j=0}^n A_jT_{n-j}.
  \end{gathered}
  \end{equation}
  The absolute value on $\Bbbk$ is trivial on $\mathbb{Q}$, so
  $|n+1|=1$. The recursion gives $\|T_n\|\leq M^n$;
  hence $T_s$ converges in operator norm for $|s|<M^{-1}$.
  The equation $\partial_sS_s=S_sA(s)$, $S_0=\operatorname{id}$, gives
  the same bound. Differentiating $S_sT_s$ and $T_sS_s$
  shows that $S_s=T_s^{-1}$.
  
  To act on arbitrary formal series, perform the same
  construction on $\widehat\mathcal{H}_b/u^N\widehat\mathcal{H}_b$.
  The bounds are independent of $N$: the operators preserve
  the $u$-adic filtration, and the quotient Gauss norms satisfy
  the same estimates. Taking inverse limits therefore defines
  mutually inverse maps on the entire completed lattices,
  including formal series that converge on no $u$-disk.
  For a shifted lattice $u^a\widehat\mathcal{H}_b$, conjugation by
  $u^a$ replaces $\delta$ in
  \eqref{eq:app-bounded-transport} by $\delta+a$.
  Since $|a|\leq1$, the bounds remain uniform in $a\in\mathbb{Z}$.
  Uniqueness in \eqref{eq:app-transport-recursion} makes these
  constructions compatible. We obtain $\Bbbk$-linear
  isomorphisms
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-transport-maps}
   T_s\colon\widehat\mathcal{H}_b^{\mathrm{mer}}
   \longrightarrow\widehat\mathcal{H}_{b_s}^{\mathrm{mer}},\qquad
   T_s(u^a\widehat\mathcal{H}_b)=u^a\widehat\mathcal{H}_{b_s}
   \quad(a\in\mathbb{Z}).
  \end{equation}
  These maps need not be $\Bbbk((u))$-linear.
  
  \medskip
  \noindent\emph{Evolution of the operators and spectral summands.}
  For an operator $O$ along the flow, differentiating its
  conjugate gives
  \[
  \partial_s(T_s^{-1}O_{b_s}T_s)
  =T_s^{-1}[\widehat\nabla_p,O]_{b_s}T_s.
  \]
  Apply this identity to $x$, $\partial_x$, and $u$.
  The commutators \eqref{eq:app-transport-commutators} and
  the initial conditions at $s=0$ yield
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-integrated-transport}
  \begin{aligned}
  x_s&:=T_s^{-1}x_{b_s}T_s=\varphi_s(x_b),\\
  \partial_{x,s}&:=T_s^{-1}\partial_{x,b_s}T_s
  =\varphi_s'(x_b)^{-1}\partial_{x,b},\\
  u_s&:=T_s^{-1}uT_s=u\varphi_s'(x_b).
  \end{aligned}
  \end{equation}
  Here $\varphi_s$ is the scalar flow in
  \eqref{eq:app-scalar-flow}. Its functions of $x_b$ are
  defined by convergent power series in $s$ on each truncated
  lattice, followed by passage to the inverse limit.
  Notice that $u_s$ denotes the transported multiplication
  operator, rather than a new scalar coordinate on the original
  fiber. 
  
  Reduction of the first identity modulo $u$ conjugates
  $K_{b_s}^{\mathrm F}$ to $\varphi_s(K_b^{\mathrm F})$.
  Thus the distinct eigenvalues of $K^{\mathrm F}$ evolve as
  $\lambda_s=\varphi_s(\lambda)$, with their multiplicities
  unchanged. Along the successive flows parametrizing $W$,
  this gives analytic labels $\lambda_\alpha(w)$.
  
  By Lemma~\ref{lem:splitting}, write
  $\widehat\mathcal{H}_b=\bigoplus_\lambda\mathcal{L}_\lambda$ for the
  $x_b$-stable spectral decomposition. Each $\mathcal{L}_\lambda$
  is preserved by $\varphi_s(x_b)$ and
  $\varphi_s'(x_b)^{\pm1}$ for small $s$. Consequently,
  \eqref{eq:app-integrated-transport} gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-transported-lattice}
   u_s\mathcal{L}_\lambda=u\mathcal{L}_\lambda,\qquad
   u\,T_s(\mathcal{L}_\lambda)=T_s(u\mathcal{L}_\lambda).
  \end{equation}
  The image $T_s(\mathcal{L}_\lambda)$ is therefore a complete
  $\Bbbk[[u]]$-submodule, stable under $x_{b_s}$.
  Lifting a basis modulo $u$ gives a finite free basis of this
  image; its reduction is the generalized
  $\varphi_s(\lambda)$-eigenspace of $K_{b_s}^{\mathrm F}$.
  These images form a direct sum. The uniqueness in
  Lemma~\ref{lem:splitting} identifies them with the spectral
  lattices at $b_s$. Localizing
  \eqref{eq:app-transported-lattice} also identifies the
  corresponding meromorphic summands under $T_s$.
  
  \medskip
  \noindent\emph{Preservation of the regular-singular factors.}
  Assume now that $\widehat\mathcal{H}_b^{\mathrm{mer}}$ is of
  unramified exponential type. Fix a spectral summand with
  eigenvalue $\lambda$. By Corollary~\ref{cor:leading-exponential},
  it is isomorphic to $\mathcal{E}^{-\lambda/u}\otimes\mathcal{R}$, with
  $\mathcal{R}$ regular singular. Choose a constant-residue basis for
  $\mathcal{R}$ as in \cite[Prop.~3.12 and Rem.~3.20(1)]{PutSinger}.
  Write $v$ for the tuple of induced basis elements of the
  exponential twist and $R$ for the constant residue matrix, so
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-initial-normal-form}
   \nabla_{\partial_u}v
   =\left(\frac{\lambda}{u^2}+\frac Ru\right)v,
   \qquad x_bv=(\lambda+uR)v.
  \end{equation}
  On this summand abbreviate $x_b$ and $\partial_{x,b}$ to
  $x$ and $\partial_x$, and put $z:=x-\lambda$.
  Then $z=u(u\partial_u+R)$ in this basis. In particular,
  $z$ strictly raises the $u$-adic order on the
  constant-residue lattice $\mathcal{L}:=\Bbbk[[u]]v$. Since
  $[\partial_x,z]=\operatorname{id}$, \eqref{eq:app-initial-normal-form}
  implies
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-centered-residue}
   z\partial_xv=(\partial_xz-\operatorname{id})v=(R-\operatorname{id})v.
  \end{equation}
  
  Set $\lambda_s:=\varphi_s(\lambda)$ and factor the
  centered scalar flow as
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-centered-flow}
   \psi_s(z):=\varphi_s(\lambda+z)-\varphi_s(\lambda)
   =a_s z h_s(z),\qquad
   a_s:=\varphi_s'(\lambda)\ne0,\qquad h_s(0)=1.
  \end{equation}
  In the notation of \eqref{eq:app-integrated-transport},
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-centered-operators}
   z_s:=x_s-\lambda_s=\psi_s(z),\qquad
   \partial_{x,s}=\psi_s'(z)^{-1}\partial_x,\qquad
   u_s=u\psi_s'(z).
  \end{equation}
  We will find a basis for the scalar action defined by $u_s$
  in which $x_s$ has the same residue matrix $R$.
  
  Because $R$ commutes with $z$ and $z$ strictly raises
  the filtration on $\mathcal{L}$, the following formal operator and
  basis tuple are well-defined:
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-corrected-basis}
   H_s(z):=h_s(z)^{R-\operatorname{id}}
   =\exp\bigl((R-\operatorname{id})\log h_s(z)\bigr),\qquad
   w:=H_s(z)v.
  \end{equation}
  The commutator $[\partial_x,z]=\operatorname{id}$ gives
  $[\partial_x,H_s(z)]=H_s'(z)$, with
  \[
  H_s'(z)=(R-\operatorname{id})H_s(z)\frac{h_s'(z)}{h_s(z)}.
  \]
  Combining this with \eqref{eq:app-centered-residue} and
  \eqref{eq:app-centered-flow}, we obtain
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-residue-calculation}
  \begin{aligned}
  z_s\partial_{x,s}w
  &=\left(\operatorname{id}+z\frac{h_s'(z)}{h_s(z)}\right)^{-1}
    z\partial_x\bigl(H_s(z)v\bigr)\\
  &=\left(\operatorname{id}+z\frac{h_s'(z)}{h_s(z)}\right)^{-1}
    \bigl(zH_s'(z)v+H_s(z)(R-\operatorname{id})v\bigr)\\
  &=(R-\operatorname{id})w.
  \end{aligned}
  \end{equation}
  Also $[\partial_{x,s},z_s]=\operatorname{id}$ and
  $u_s\partial_{x,s}=\operatorname{id}$, by
  \eqref{eq:app-centered-operators}. Hence
  \eqref{eq:app-residue-calculation} gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-transported-normal-form}
   z_sw=u_s(\partial_{x,s}z_s)w=u_sRw,
   \qquad x_sw=(\lambda_s+u_sR)w.
  \end{equation}
  
  It remains to check that this operator calculation produces
  an actual $\Bbbk((u))$-basis at $b_s$. By
  \eqref{eq:app-corrected-basis}, $w\equiv v\pmod{u\mathcal{L}}$,
  while \eqref{eq:app-centered-operators} gives, for $k\geq0$,
  \[
  u_s(u^k\mathcal{L})=u^{k+1}\mathcal{L},\qquad
  u_s=a_su\pmod{\text{operators raising the $u$-adic order by two}}.
  \]
  Successive reduction modulo powers of $u$ therefore expresses
  each element of $\mathcal{L}$ uniquely as a formal series in $u_s$
  with coefficients in the $\Bbbk$-span of the entries of $w$.
  The lattice $\mathcal{L}$ is commensurable with the original spectral
  lattice, and \eqref{eq:app-transport-maps} ensures that $T_s$
  is continuous for their $u$-adic topologies. Since
  $T_su_s=uT_s$, the tuple $T_sw$ is a
  $\Bbbk[[u]]$-basis of $T_s(\mathcal{L})$ and a
  $\Bbbk((u))$-basis of the transported summand.
  Applying $T_s$ to \eqref{eq:app-transported-normal-form}
  and dividing by $u^2$ gives
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-final-normal-form}
   \nabla_{\partial_u}(T_sw)
   =\left(\frac{\lambda_s}{u^2}+\frac Ru\right)(T_sw).
  \end{equation}
  Thus \eqref{eq:app-final-normal-form} identifies the summand
  at $b_s$ with $\mathcal{E}^{-\lambda_s/u}\otimes\mathcal{R}$: its
  regular-singular factor has the same constant residue matrix
  as in \eqref{eq:app-initial-normal-form}.
  
  Apply this argument to every initial spectral summand and
  then to the successive generating flows parametrizing $W$.
  After shrinking their parameter polydisk, these identifications
  hold throughout $W$ and give \eqref{eq:app-constant-factors}.
  This proves (iii).

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:compatible-persistence}
  The formal-persistence conclusion also holds for an additional
  F-bundle $(\widetilde\mathcal{H},\widetilde\nabla)$ on the same leaf
  $W$, not necessarily maximal, provided that its action and
  residual endomorphism satisfies
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:app-compatible-action}
   \widetilde\mu(X_p)=p(\widetilde K^{\mathrm F}),
   \qquad p\in\Bbbk[z],\qquad
   X_p=p_\circ(\mathsf{Eu}^{\mathrm F}).
  \end{equation}
  Here $\mathsf{Eu}^{\mathrm F}$ is the Euler field of the original
  maximal F-bundle, and $\widetilde\mu$ and
  $\widetilde K^{\mathrm F}$ are defined by
  \eqref{eq:F-residual-action} for the additional bundle.
  If $\widehat{\widetilde\mathcal{H}}_b^{\mathrm{mer}}$ is of
  unramified exponential type, its regular-singular factors are
  locally constant up to isomorphism along $W$, with eigenvalues
  matched by the flows above.
  
  Indeed, maximality was used to construct the tangent algebra
  and the leaf. Condition~\eqref{eq:app-compatible-action}
  allows us to apply Lemma~\ref{lem:app-transport-operators}
  to the additional bundle. The parallel transport and
  constant-residue calculation then apply without change.
  If the additional bundle is a super vector bundle, all these
  operators are even, and the argument applies to each parity
  separately.
